title: Why My Demo Clips Film the Real Site, Not a Fake One | vitalii.no
description:
Every earlier feature-demo clip I made was built from a synthetic harness -- a standalone page that faked the component in isolation. It looked plausible but it wasn't proof of anything: the real site could be broken and the demo would still play. I wanted a recorder that could only produce a clip if the live feature actually worked.

I wrote a Playwright script that opens a real Chromium tab against the production vitalii.no site, clears the cookie consent banner from local storage so it never appears mid-recording, then drives the actual page: opens the target feature, waits for real network idle, and performs the interactions being demonstrated. An overlay injected into the live page paints the cursor and click effects on top of the real render, so the recording shows genuine site behavior with added visual polish rather than a re-created one. The raw capture is retimed to 0.67x afterward for a calmer pace.

Feature demo clips now double as a live smoke test -- if the recorder produces a clip, the feature it shows actually works on production, not just in an isolated mockup.
